question: Assume today is 2026-09-12. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of passengers at London Heathrow Airport in September 2026, as reported in Heathrow's monthly traffic statistics.

target.what: Total passengers passing through London Heathrow Airport (LHR) during September 2026, as reported in Heathrow's monthly traffic statistics (terminal and transit passengers counted per airport traffic convention)
target.publisher: Heathrow Airport Limited (monthly traffic statistics / operational figures)
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-12 cutoff, so no September 2026 actuals exist; must be forecast from prior Septembers, 2026 year-to-date monthly figures, capacity schedules, and demand signals. Definitional issues: Heathrow counts passengers including transit/connecting passe

candidates.hypothesis: September passenger totals in prior years (2015-2019, 2022-2025) establish the seasonal level and September's typical ratio to adjacent months and to annual totals; applying the September share of annual traffic or the September-to-August ratio to a 2026 base gives the target.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly passenger totals for September 2015-2019 and 2022-2025, plus August and October of the same years; annual totals for those years. Minimum: September 2024 and September 2025 totals and the September share of annual passengers.
search_hints: Heathrow monthly traffic statistics September passengers

candidates.hypothesis: 2026 year-to-date monthly passenger totals (Jan-Aug 2026) published before the cutoff, compared with the same months in 2025, give a growth rate that can be carried into September 2026 with a seasonal adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly passenger totals January-August 2026 and January-August 2025; any reported year-on-year percentage changes. Minimum: latest two or three months of 2026 with year-on-year comparisons.
search_hints: Heathrow monthly traffic 2026 year on year

candidates.perspective: Airport slot coordinator and airline schedules
candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 seat capacity at Heathrow (departing seats from schedules, doubled for arrivals, adjusted for load factor and transit) bounds and predicts realised passengers: passengers ≈ 2 × departing seats × load factor × (1 + transit share).
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow departing seat capacity for September 2026 from ACL slot coordination or OAG/Cirium schedules; achieved load factors for Heathrow or UK long-haul/short-haul; transit passenger share. Minimum: September 2026 scheduled departing seats and a plausible load factor.

candidates.perspective: UK Civil Aviation Authority airport statistics
candidates.hypothesis: CAA monthly airport statistics report Heathrow terminal passengers on a comparable basis; the CAA series can validate or substitute for Heathrow's own monthly figures and provide September seasonality.
candidates.data_to_find: CAA monthly airport passenger data for Heathrow for September 2024, September 2025 and any 2026 months available before cutoff; definitional notes on transit passengers.
search_hints: CAA airport statistics Heathrow monthly passengers
UK CAA terminal passengers Heathrow September

candidates.hypothesis: Heathrow's own full-year 2026 passenger guidance and any third-quarter outlook, combined with the historical September share of annual traffic, yields a September estimate; airline capacity guidance for winter 2026 constrains it.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow plc full-year 2026 passenger guidance or trading statements before 2026-09-12; IATA/ACI Europe or airline (BA, Virgin) capacity commentary for September 2026. Minimum: Heathrow 2026 annual passenger forecast.

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 traffic is shifted by specific events: strikes, ATC disruptions, weather, route suspensions, or new routes; measurable exposure (cancelled flights, days affected) adjusts the baseline estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Reports of Heathrow strikes, ATC outages, airline route changes, or capacity cuts affecting September 2026, dated before 2026-09-12; any announced schedule reductions for autumn 2026.
search_hints: UK air traffic control disruption September 2026

candidates.hypothesis: September is typically a transition month with passengers between August peak and October; the September-to-August and September-to-annual ratios are stable enough to transfer across years, so a 2026 August actual (if published) times the historical ratio gives September.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical September/August passenger ratios for Heathrow 2015-2019 and 2022-2025; August 2026 actual if published before cutoff. Minimum: three years of September and August totals.
search_hints: Heathrow monthly passengers August September comparison

candidates.hypothesis: Air transport movements (ATMs) at Heathrow times average passengers per movement gives passengers; September 2026 ATMs can be estimated from schedule or prior Septembers and multiplied by a stable passengers-per-ATM ratio.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly air transport movements for September 2022-2025 and any 2026 months; average passengers per ATM implied by passenger/ATM totals. Minimum: September 2025 ATMs and passengers.
search_hints: Heathrow air transport movements monthly statistics

assumptions.name: September 2026 realised load factor

assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 load factor is near the annual forecast level.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp load-factor drop from disruption or a surge to 85%+.

assumptions.name: Arrivals-to-departures seat multiplier
assumptions.rationale: Departing seats must be doubled to include arriving seats. Heathrow is a slot-constrained two-runway airport where arrivals and departures are near-balanced, so the multiplier is close to 2; the range allows for slight asymmetry in the schedule.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 schedule has near-equal arriving and departing seat capacity.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large arrival/departure imbalance in the September 2026 schedule.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: September 2025 total (7,348k) scaled by the August 2026 vs August 2025 ratio. August 2026 level 7,866,510 (p179) vs August 2025 8,035,996 (p184) gives the most recent observed YoY factor. Shared dependency: both August values come from the same HAL release; failure mode is that August seasonality differs from September.

methods.label: m3

a1.role: September 2026 year-on-year change factor relative to September 2025

methods.rationale: Direct YoY scaling of the September 2025 record total by a 2026 change factor grounded in the 2026 YTD pattern (Jan +2.2%, Apr -5.3%, Jul -1.5%, Aug ~-2%). Shared dependency with m1 on the 2025 September base; failure mode is that the 2026 change differs from the YTD average.

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks
weight_basis.m2: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m2.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

baseline.rule: seasonal naive: the target's value for the same calendar period last year

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m2
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: unit check: the formula's result is 'seat/month' (seat/month * 1 * 1 = seat/month), which is not a 'person' quantity: you judged that it does not fit the target unit 'person': The formula gives seats per month, a count of seats, not passengers; a seat is not the same kind of quantity as a person, so it cannot be converted to the target unit person.

kept.name: September 2026 YoY change vs September 2025
kept.rationale: 2026 has been roughly flat to slightly down: Jan +2.2%, Feb +1.9%, Apr -5.3% (Middle East shock), Jul -1.5%, Aug level implies ~-2%. The Middle East shock has largely unwound by August. September 2025 was a record (7,348k), so a small positive-to-slightly-negative change is plausible; central +0.5%
kept.applies_when: September 2026 demand tracks the 2026 YTD pattern with no new major disruption.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a renewed Middle East/ATC shock or a strong autumn demand surge.

kept.name: September 2026 realised load factor
kept.rationale: Steer base case 80.5%, HAL P50 81.2%, 2024 actual 80.7%; Airlines Base 84.7% is an outlier. September is a shoulder month with high but not peak load factors. Central 80.5% with range spanning the credible forecasts.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 load factor is near the annual forecast level.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp load-factor drop from disruption or a surge to 85%+.

kept.name: Arrivals-to-departures seat multiplier
kept.rationale: Departing seats must be doubled to include arriving seats. Heathrow is a slot-constrained two-runway airport where arrivals and departures are near-balanced, so the multiplier is close to 2; the range allows for slight asymmetry in the schedule.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 schedule has near-equal arriving and departing seat capacity.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a large arrival/departure imbalance in the September 2026 schedule.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
